notes: ACCESS: bloomingdales.com (a Macy's Inc. sister property, same Nuxt/Akamai stack as macys.com/S.N.74) hard-blocks every live-fetch route tried: direct requests (403 'Access Denied' Akamai custom-deny page), an 18-profile curl_cffi impersonation sweep (chrome99-131, safari15_3-18_0, safari18_0_ios, edge99/101 -- 3 Safari profiles briefly returned an Akamai *behavioral* JS sensor challenge instead of a hard deny, but that still yields no page content and the IP was hard-blocked again within 2 more requests), WebFetch (403), r.jina.ai (own Cloudflare 'Just a moment' challenge, confirmed generic/unrelated to this target by testing r.jina.ai/https://example.com), translate.goog (proxies through to the same origin Access-Denied page), PowerShell Invoke-WebRequest (403), and public CORS proxies (corsproxy.io 403, allorigins.win/thingproxy timeout/DNS fail). m.bloomingdales.com and www1.bloomingdales.com are identically blocked. By contrast macys.com was fetched successfully in the same session with zero blocking, confirming this is a Bloomingdale's-specific WAF policy, not a general network problem. Given DO-NOT-USE-BROWSER-AUTOMATION and no unprotected side door found (robots.txt/sitemap also 403), live qty verification was not achievable this session -- every qty below is null with a MANUAL REVIEW flag per the null-is-a-correct-answer rule. STRUCTURE (nav tree, category IDs, breadcrumbs) was instead reconstructed from Wayback Machine snapshots spanning 2026-01 to 2026-06-09 (most no older than ~7 months, several from within the last 2-3 months), which is permitted for structure only, per rule, never for counts -- so every Wayback-observed count is quoted in 'evidence' purely as unverified historical context, explicitly NOT used as the reported qty. The site's own Nuxt page-data (same family as Macy's totalResults, migrated from an older window.__INITIAL_STATE__ format to a newer data-nuxt-data='nuxt-app' devalue-array payload sometime around April 2026) and its 'Decorative Accessory Type'/'Lighting Type' facets (each with per-value counts and its own filterable URL, e.g. /Lighting_type_ea/Chandelier) supplied the category/product-type breakdown used to build rows below. TAXONOMY: Home Decor hub (id=1001539, breadcrumb Home>Home Decor) presents exactly 10 mega-nav children as of the 2026-06-09 snapshot: Bowls/Trays/Vases, Candles & Home Fragrances, Curtains & Window Treatments, Coffee Table Books, Decorative Pillows & Throws, Decorative Objects, Mirrors & Wall Art, Lighting, Picture Frames, Rugs -- Curtains/Coffee-Table-Books/Pillows&Throws/Rugs excluded as textiles/books, not decor. Mirrors & Wall Art (id=1001546) has exactly two site-defined children, Mirrors (id=1005865, 138) and Wall Art (id=1005868, 85) -- kept both as leaves under a parent row. Lighting (id=1001009, hub total 726) has NO further crawlable sub-category pages, only a 'Lighting Type' facet -- broken into 9 product-type leaves (Chandelier, Desk Lamp, Floor Lamp, Flush Mount, Outdoor Lighting [Rule 0.1 room/location branch kept], Pendant, Semi-Flush Mount, Table Lamp, Wall Lamps and Sconces); 'Ceiling Fan' (36) dropped as a fan, not a fixture, per the standing exclusion. Bowls/Trays/Vases (id=1001541, hub total 1413) similarly has no sub-pages, only its own 'Decorative Accessory Type' facet -- kept the three genuinely-its-own product types Bowls(290)/Trays(224)/Vases(917); dropped same-facet's Books/Judaica/Window-Curtains/Plants&Planters/Holiday-Decor plus the small cross-tagged Mirrors&WallArt/PictureFrames/Candlesticks slivers (2-14 items each) that belong to other branches (Rule 0.6: facet cross-tag, not a genuine second branch). Decorative Objects (id=1001543, hub total 557, page title literally 'Decorative Objects') is a mixed department-store bucket -- kept only 'Collectibles' (319, dominated by Figurines&Objects/Sculptures per its own Collectibles-Type sub-facet) and 'Home Accents' (152) as genuine decor; dropped Books(38)/Judaica(6)/Window-Curtains(7)/Plants&Florals(55 faux-plant exclusion)/Jewelry-Boxes(27, personal accessory not decor)/Desk-Accessories(31, ambiguous office-supply overlap, dropped conservatively) and small cross-tag slivers. Picture Frames (id=1001547, 530) is a clean single-type category, kept whole. CANDLES: Candles & Home Fragrances (id=1001542, hub total 2192) has 5 children -- Votives(id=1272602, confirmed via sampled page text as scented 'Votive Candles', 22 scent/23 fragrance keyword hits, 0 'unscented' -- dropped), Candle Sets(dropped, gift/scent bundles), Candles(id=1005851, dropped, scented), Diffusers(dropped, home fragrance), and Candleholders(id=1005853, 327) -- kept ONLY Candleholders as genuine unscented decor per the standing candle-holder carve-out. A near-duplicate node 'Modern Candle Holders & Candlesticks' (id=1144096, 237, page title 'Modern Candle Holders & Candlesticks') was found at an older Wayback timestamp but is absent from the current (2026-04) Candles&Fragrances nav tree and its own facet self-tags 237 of 237 as 'Candlesticks' (a near-subset signature of Candleholders' own Candlesticks facet value of 229/327) -- treated as a superseded/consolidated duplicate of the current Candleholders node per Rule 0.6 and not emitted as a second row. DROPPED AS MIXED, NOT AS A ROOM EXCLUSION (Rule 0.4): 'Bathroom Decor & Accessories' (id=1063260, 209) and its near-identical child 'Bathroom Decor' (id=1005704, 208, breadcrumb Home>Bath>Bathroom Decor&Accessories>Bathroom Decor) were investigated in good faith (Rule 0.4 explicitly wants bathroom mirrors/lighting included), but raw page-text keyword sampling of the saved Wayback HTML showed substantial non-decor content mixed in alongside genuine decor (Shower Curtain x16, Soap Dispenser x9, Tissue x38, Toothbrush x11, Scale x4, Hamper x7 vs Mirror x44/Wall Art x3/Tray x30) with no facet-level breakdown available in this snapshot's format to isolate a clean decor-only subset -- per 'mixed roll-ups: drop them, don't pad, inspect actual titles first' this whole branch was dropped rather than guessed at; flagged for a future worker with live access to re-attempt. No dedicated 'Clocks' category exists anywhere in Bloomingdale's nav (only 'Alarm Clock' as a Personal-Care/Electronics facet value, correctly out of scope) -- a genuine absence, not an oversight, unlike Macy's which does carry a Clocks node.
